key_insight: A stochastic parcel model links cloud microphysics to emergent bands, cells, and wave networks through dynamic inertia and amplitude-dependent frequency shifts.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to representing unresolved microphysics in cloud models and identifying fluctuation statistics for calibration against large-eddy simulations.
method: Model cloud-water and rain-water anomalies as stochastic parcel jumps.
Combine screened environmental coupling with cubic oscillatory dynamics.
Close moments to derive a pseudoparabolic Ginzburg–Landau equation and analyze pattern stability.
evidence_signal: Analytical stability criteria and numerical integrations show twist-driven transitions from bands to defect-rich waves, alongside cellular and spiral patterns without twist.
watch_item: Moment closure omits fluctuation statistics that require calibration; the abstract reports no validation against observations or large-eddy simulations.
paper_title: Emergent cloud patterns from stochastic jump models of parcel microphysics
